title: Phrasal verbs 8: up (2)
subtitle: bring up / cheer up / put up with
summary: Learn more phrasal verbs with up: bringing up a topic, cheering somebody up, doing a house up and putting up with problems.

lesson.heading: bring up, come up, make up
lesson.text: **bring up** a topic = introduce it in a conversation. **come up** = be introduced in a conversation. **come up with** an idea = produce it. **make something up** = invent something that is not true.

examples.text: I don't want to hear any more about this. Please don't **bring it up** again.
Some interesting things **came up** in our discussion yesterday.
Sarah is very creative. She's always **coming up with** new ideas.
What Kevin told you about himself wasn't true. He **made it all up**.

lesson.heading: cheer up, save up, clear up
lesson.text: **cheer up** = be happier; **cheer somebody up** = make them feel happier. **save up for something** = save money to buy it. **clear up** = become bright (about the weather).

examples.text: You look so sad! **Cheer up!**
Helen is depressed. What can we do to **cheer her up**?
Dan is **saving up for** a trip to New Zealand.
It was raining when I got up, but it **cleared up** later.

lesson.heading: blow up, tear up, beat up
lesson.text: **blow up** = explode; **blow something up** = destroy it with a bomb. **tear something up** = tear it into pieces. **beat somebody up** = hit them repeatedly so that they are badly hurt.

examples.text: The engine caught fire and **blew up**.
The bridge **was blown up** during the war.
I didn't read the letter. I just **tore it up** and threw it away.
A friend of mine was attacked and **beaten up**. He had to go to hospital.

lesson.heading: break up, split up, do up
lesson.text: **break up** or **split up (with somebody)** = separate. **do up** a coat or a shoelace = fasten or tie it. **do up** a building or a room = repair and improve it.

examples.text: I'm surprised to hear that Kate and Paul have **split up**. They seemed very happy together.
It's quite cold. **Do up** your coat before you go out.
The kitchen looks great now that it **has been done up**.

lesson.heading: look up and put up with
lesson.text: **look something up** in a dictionary = find the information there. **put up with something** = tolerate a difficult situation or person.

examples.text: If you don't know the meaning of a word, you can **look it up** in a dictionary.
We live on a busy road, so we have to **put up with** a lot of noise from the traffic.

lesson.heading: hold up and mix up
lesson.text: **hold up** a person or a plan = delay them. **mix up** people or things (or **get them mixed up**) = think that one is the other.

examples.text: Don't wait for me. I don't want to **hold you up**.
Plans to build a new factory **have been held up** because of financial problems.
The two brothers look very similar. People often **mix them up**.
examples.note: or ... People often get them mixed up.

lesson.text: *do up* has two meanings: fasten something (do up your coat) and repair something (they did up the old house).

exercises.prompt: Match each beginning with the words that go with it.

pairs.left: He was angry and tore up
I think you should do up
We had to put up with

exercises.prompt: The weather was horrible this morning, but it's ___ now.
exercises.explanation: clear up = become bright, stop raining.

exercises.prompt: Lisa arrived late and said sorry: she was ___ in the traffic.
They bought an old house and ___. It's really nice now.
exercises.explanation: do up a building = repair and improve it.

exercises.prompt: Joe was really depressed. We took him out for a meal to ___.
exercises.explanation: cheer somebody up = make them feel happier.

exercises.prompt: The ship ___ and sank. The cause of the explosion was never discovered.
Robert and Tina aren't together any more. They've ___.
exercises.explanation: split up (or break up) = separate, end a relationship.

exercises.prompt: I turned up for the party on the wrong day. I got the dates ___.
exercises.explanation: get things mixed up = think one is the other.

exercises.prompt: I don't know what this word means. I'll have to ___.
exercises.explanation: look a word up = find it in a dictionary.

exercises.prompt: The problem was complicated, but we managed to ___ a solution.
exercises.explanation: come up with something = produce an idea or a solution.

exercises.statement: What Kevin told you about himself wasn't true. He made it all up.
exercises.explanation: Correct. make something up = invent something that is not true.

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in order to explain why you hear so much traffic noise.
exercises.answer: We live on a busy road, so we have to put up with a lot of noise.
exercises.explanation: put up with something = tolerate a difficult situation.
